objects.description: One line of the chart of accounts. Category and holder_id together are its identity, and it is opened lazily by its first posting rather than because its holder registered.

fields.name: code
fields.description: The account number a chart of accounts is laid out by, such as 1000 for cash. Supplied by the caller and never minted here; optional, and unique across the ledger when it is given.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The account's title as a ledger prints it, such as 'Cash at bank'. Free text the caller chooses.

fields.name: category
fields.description: What sort of account this is, in the calling domain's own words — a member's account, a paybill's basket, a school's fee account. Deliberately open: which categories exist is the part that differs between a membership organisation, a school and a token ledger, so this module never validates it against a fixed list.

fields.name: type
fields.description: The account's place in the accounting equation, and so its normal balance. The one closed vocabulary here, because it is double-entry theory itself rather than a decision any one domain gets to make differently.

fields.name: holder_id
fields.description: The subject this subsidiary account is kept for — a member, a paybill, a student, a wallet address. An opaque id the caller supplies and interprets; this module never reads it for meaning, only for identity.

fields.name: opened_at
fields.description: When the first posting opened the account. Written by the store, never by a caller.

fields.name: closed_at
fields.description: When the account was closed. The only value on an account that ever changes, and it is refused while a balance remains.

indexes.name: identity
indexes.description: Enforces one account per (category, holder_id), which is what makes opening idempotent rather than a pre-check-then-insert race.

indexes.name: code
indexes.description: Backs the refusal of a code some other account already carries. Not declared unique, because every account without a code stores the empty string rather than null and they would all collide on one constraint.

indexes.name: opened
indexes.description: Orders the account listing oldest-opened first.

objects.description: One journal entry: an amount debited to exactly one account and credited to exactly one other. Append-only — there is no update and no delete, and a mistake is corrected by a new entry naming the original in reverses_entry_id.

fields.name: posted_at
fields.description: When it hit the books. Written by the store, never by a caller.

fields.name: occurred_at
fields.description: When the underlying event happened. A read that orders a ledger orders on this, falling back to posted_at where it is absent.

fields.name: debit_account_id
fields.description: The account debited. Every entry names both sides; there is no one-sided posting in this ledger.

fields.name: credit_account_id
fields.description: The account credited, for the same amount, which is what makes the entry balance.

fields.name: amount
fields.description: The amount posted to both sides, in the deployment's smallest denominated unit, always positive. Which side is which is the two accounts, never a sign, so no posting can change the sum of every balance in the ledger.

fields.name: document_kind
fields.description: What sort of source document caused the posting — an invoice, a receipt, a statement import — in the calling domain's own words. Open for the same reason category is: this module enforces that every entry names one, never which ones exist.

fields.name: document_id
fields.description: The source document that caused the posting.

fields.name: actor_id
fields.description: Who or what caused the posting, never only a role. The ledger is an accountability surface, so this is required.

fields.name: narration
fields.description: The sentence the ledger reads back against this entry; on a correction, the reason for the reversal.

fields.name: reverses_entry_id
fields.description: The entry this one corrects, or empty. The original is never touched, and an entry may be reversed at most once — a second reversal would drift the ledger off zero-sum.

indexes.name: debit_account
indexes.description: Reads the debit side of one account's ledger, which every balance and listing folds.

indexes.name: credit_account
indexes.description: Reads the credit side of the same.

indexes.name: reverses
indexes.description: Answers 'has this entry already been reversed' without scanning the ledger, which is the check that keeps a correction from being applied twice.
